title: Spreading a Reinstated Balance After Recent Consecutive Misses
content:
**Revenue Cycle Policy Manual — Patient Payment Plans: spread of a reinstated balance after recent consecutive misses**

**Clause.** The installments the reinstated balance is spread over depend on how the plan fell behind: on a plan with 2 or more installments recorded missed less than 3 whole months before today that was accepted at least 6 whole months before today, they are the whole installments the pre-default installment needs to clear the reinstated balance, the quotient rounded down; on a plan with 2 or more such missed installments accepted less than 6 whole months before today, that quotient rounded up; on any other plan, the installments still to fall due under the term.

**Terms.**
- *Installments recorded missed less than 3 whole months before today* — missed-installment lines on the plan ledger dated within that span.
- *Pre-default installment* — the regular monthly installment the plan carried when it defaulted, as the plan record shows it.
- *The quotient* — the reinstated balance divided by the pre-default installment.
- *Seasoning* — whole months from the plan's acceptance date to today.

## Determination table

| Missed-installment lines in the last 3 whole months | Accepted at least 6 whole months before today | Installments the reinstated balance is spread over |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | Yes | The quotient, rounded down to a whole installment |
| 2 or more | No | The quotient, rounded up to a whole installment |
| 0 or 1 | Yes or No | The installments still to fall due under the term |

## Hypothetical figures (pre-default installment 90.00)

| Reinstated balance | Quotient | Seasoned plan, 2 recent misses | Newer plan, 2 recent misses |
|---|---|---|---|
| 630.00 | 7 exactly | 7 | 7 |
| 650.00 | 7.22… | 7 | 8 |
| 700.00 | 7.77… | 7 | 8 |

A plan with two missed-installment lines, one dated 1 month ago and the other 4 whole months ago, has only one line inside the 3-month span; its balance is spread over the installments still to fall due under the term.
